pr.title: Cut the test suite from nine minutes to about one
pr.head: 2598bf8ea2aa4b2161eb84991b67bf479d054f6b

summary: Projector's Python test suite took about nine minutes to run serially. It runs on every push, before every fix, and again in review. Most of that time went to starting processes. The same Git fixture was rebuilt with a dozen git processes before every test. The site server helper waited out a half-second poll on every request. Fixed sleeps and timeouts ran to their full length.
This pull request changes only tests, the gate command, and the documentation that names it. No file under src/ changes. It does three things:

1. Builds each expensive fixture once and copies it. tests/scratch.py adds copy_of, which runs a fixture builder once per process and gives each test its own copy. It rewrites the absolute paths Git recorded so they point into the copy.
  2. Runs the suite in parallel. python3 -m tests is a standard-library runner. It splits each test class into chunks of up to eight tests and runs python3 -m unittest on each chunk in its own worker process, one worker per CPU. It becomes the gate in AGENTS.md, docs/develop.md, and the Check workflow.
  3. Deletes tests that caught nothing, and shortens waits. It deletes tests that restated CSS or argparse choices, pinned a removed command, or checked the same behavior as another test through the same code path, or merges them into table tests. Projector's testing guide sets these rules.
The head merges main twice. The second merge moves main's two new skill-text tests into SkillTextTests, the class where this branch now keeps the skill-text tests.

groups.title: The parallel runner and copied fixtures
groups.kicker: Two new helpers under tests/ that every other change builds on
intro: copy_of(build) runs build once per process in a template directory, then copies the template for each test with shutil.copytree. Git writes absolute paths into a repository's config, for a remote's URL and insteadOf rules, and into a linked worktree's gitdir and .git files. So relocate replaces the template's path with the copy's in those files. A remote that names a sibling repository then names the copy's sibling, and no two tests share a repository.

python3 -m tests discovers the suite in the parent process and groups test ids by class. It splits each class into chunks of eight. A thread pool with one worker per CPU runs each chunk as python3 -m unittest <ids>. Each worker imports tests/__init__.py, which gives it a temporary root of its own, so workers share only the machine.

checks.text: A test class's chunks run in different processes. So anything a class caches, such as copy_of's templates or FileHeaderTests.built, is built once per chunk rather than once per run. That costs time, not correctness.

files.note: The runner: discovery, chunking, the worker pool, and the summary line.

checks.text: The loader turns a module that fails to import into a _FailedTest. The runner runs it by name, so its chunk fails and the run exits 1. I checked this by reading how unittest.loader names failed imports, both in discovery and in a run by name.
relocate skips symlinks. A fixture that made an absolute symlink inside its template would give every copy a link back into the template. None of the fixtures that use copy_of make a symlink.

groups.title: The gate runs the new runner
groups.kicker: The documented gate and CI switch from unittest discover to python3 -m tests
intro: The Check workflow, the gate list in AGENTS.md, and docs/develop.md now run PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m tests. CLAUDE.md is a link to AGENTS.md, so it changes too. docs/develop.md also documents -j, -v, and running one module, class, or test. python3 -m unittest still runs any part of the suite in one process.

files.note: Only the test step's command changes. No secret or permission changes.

groups.title: Fixtures built once and copied
groups.kicker: Review, relay, release, summary, and projector tests start from a copied template
intro: Each of these files moves its Git setup from setUp into a builder at module level, which copy_of runs once. The rest of each test stays as it was. Some files also merge two tests that built the same fixture to check related facts. For example, the summary test of a publish that retries after losing a race now also checks that the retry keeps the head's attributes.

files.note: The test copies the relay scratch directory, which holds each machine's checkout and the fake keychain and codex tools. The ref-flood test patches OPEN_LIMIT to 2 and plants 3 messages instead of 100.

checks.text: The keychain fallback test now gives the fake secret-tool 0.2s to report "no secret service". It passed 20 of 20 runs at load averages of 300 to 560 on 12 cores, and it passed in the full parallel run.

groups.title: Tests removed or merged
groups.kicker: Duplicates, restated code, and pinned decisions go; facets of one outcome become table tests
intro: Each test that this group deletes falls into one of two kinds. Some restate a literal the code holds, such as a CSS rule, a hex color, or argparse's choice list. Others check a behavior that another test already checks through the same code path. For example, every Projector reader of a verdict marker goes through verdict_marker. So the version-less and approved marker cases in VerdictMarkerTests cover status, dismissal, and the site, and the copies of those cases in each of those places are gone.

Ten interdiff rule tests each paid for a full incremental-review fixture. They become one table test. Its baseline head passes every rule. Each case changes one input, checks the refusal, and restores the input. The site's status and stack-segment logic is now called directly, and the test suite keeps one end-to-end case for each path through the build.

checks.text: FileHeaderTests.build caches one build for each set of arguments, for the life of the process, and returns a deep copy of it. That is correct only while no test changes the checkout before it builds, and none does at this head.

groups.title: Shorter and event-driven waits
groups.kicker: Fixed joins and long timeouts give way to waits on the event itself
intro: The agent registration race test used to join the second registration for half a second. It now waits until that registration reaches the names' lock. The inbox lock tests now hold the lock on a file descriptor of their own, so they start no subprocess, and they wait 0.1s instead of 0.3s. The installer test puts the real interpreter first on PATH, so a slow python3 shim from a version manager does not run.
